t: Minimum Operations to Make Median of Array Equal to K
o: Each operation changes one element by ±1; we want the median (upper-middle element of the sorted array) to become k. In Example 1, sorted [2,5,5,6,8] has median 6; lowering the two elements above... concretely we reduce the two 5s toward 4 at cost 2. In Example 2 we raise 5→7 (twice) and 6→7 (once), cost 3. In Example 3 the median already equals 4. Greedy insight: only elements on the 'wrong side' of the median position matter. If the current median exceeds k, decrease elements from the median position leftward while they exceed k; if it is below k, increase elements rightward while they are below k. Elements beyond those runs need no change, since moving them would not affect the median.
k: Sort the array; the median sits at index m = ⌊n/2⌋ (upper middle for even n).
If nums[m] > k, pay Σ(max(0, nums[i] − k)) for i from m downward while nums[i] > k; symmetrically for nums[m] < k going upward.
Elements outside that contiguous run are irrelevant to the median and cost nothing.

a.i: After sorting, making the median equal k only requires fixing the chain of elements between the median position and k's 'side'. Decreasing nums[m] down to k may expose nums[m−1] as the new median, which then also must be ≤-adjusted if it exceeds k, and so on — hence the contiguous run. Each unit of adjustment costs exactly one operation, so the answer is the sum of absolute differences over that run.
s: Sort nums; set m = n // 2 and ans = 0.
If nums[m] > k: for i = m down to 0 while nums[i] > k, add nums[i] − k.
Else if nums[m] < k: for i = m up to n−1 while nums[i] < k, add k − nums[i].
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; the accumulation scans at most n elements.
a.sp: O(1) extra space beyond the sort.

w: Use this single approach — sorting is essentially mandatory and the greedy run is provably minimal (each adjusted element must cross k for the median to change, and moving non-run elements is pure waste). Pitfalls: for even n the median is the larger middle element, i.e. index n/2 after sorting; use 64-bit accumulators since costs can reach ~10¹⁴; and note the two branches are mutually exclusive. Follow-ups: minimize operations to make the median at least / at most k, or handle weighted elements (then a weighted-median / sweep argument applies).
